title: OOM triage command cheatsheet & incident breadcrumbs
content:
Purpose:
A compact, copy-paste friendly cheatsheet for triaging GPU OOMs and library/driver mismatches on Redwood infra. Keep as a personal scratchpad during live incident work — messy, quick notes, hypothesis log.

High-level approach (order of operations during a live hit):
1) Capture process & container context (PID, container id, image, command).
2) Snapshot GPU state (nvidia-smi, nvml dumps, dmesg).
3) Record exact CUDA/CUDNN/libcuda/libnvidia versions and LD_LIBRARY_PATH/LD_PRELOAD state.
4) Reproduce minimal: try run with a tiny batch / reduced sequence length.
5) If non-repro, collect continuous traces (strace / perf / nvprof / pgrep + gdb) and escalate.

Quick commands (copy-paste):
- identify PIDs using GPU (host):
  sudo lsof /dev/nvidia* | awk '{print $2" "$1}' | sort -u
  sudo fuser -v /dev/nvidia*
  nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv

- container context (docker / containerd):
  docker ps --filter "status=running" --format 'table {{.ID}}	{{.Image}}	{{.Names}}'
  docker inspect --format='{{.Id}} {{.Config.Image}} {{range .Config.Cmd}}{{.}} {{end}}' <cid>
  ctr -n k8s.io tasks ls | grep <node-pid> (containerd)
  cat /proc/<pid>/mountinfo | grep nvidia (check mounted lib paths)

- GPU snapshot (fast):
  nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,POWER -f /tmp/nvidia-smi-snapshot.txt
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=uuid,name,driver_version,memory.total,memory.free --format=csv
  nvtop (live)

- NVML quick core dump (if NVML supports):
  python -c "import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); print(pynvml.nvmlSystemGetDriverVersion())" 2>&1 | tee /tmp/nvml-driver.txt

- dmesg / kernel: filter for GPU events (pagefault, OOM, mm errors):
  sudo dmesg -T | egrep -i "NVRM|nvidia|GPU|oom|pagefault|mmu" | tail -n 200 | tee /tmp/gpu-dmesg.txt

- check loaded libraries for the process (LD_LIB paths & versions):
  sudo cat /proc/<pid>/maps | egrep "libcuda|libnvidia|libcudnn|libcublas" | sed -E 's/.* (//.*)/\1/' | sort -u
  strings $(ldd /path/to/binary | egrep -o '/[^ ]+libcuda[^ ]*') | head -n 20
  sudo ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* /usr/lib/nvidia-* || true
  readelf -a /path/to/libcuda.so | egrep "SONAME|Version" || true

- environment capture for process:
  sudo tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<pid>/environ | egrep -i "LD_LIBRARY_PATH|LD_PRELOAD|CUDA|CUDNN|NV_CUDASM|NVIDIA" | tee /tmp/env-<pid>.txt

- reproducibility quick test (reduce memory pressure):
  export BATCH=1
  export SEQ=32
  python serve.py --model small --batch_size $BATCH --max_seq_len $SEQ 2>&1 | tee reproduce-out.txt

- force library mismatch check (sandboxed):
  docker run --rm --gpus all -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/weird/lib my-inference-image:staging python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())"

- collect a complete process trace (use sparingly on prod):
  sudo strace -f -p <pid> -o /tmp/strace-<pid>.log & sleep 10; sudo kill -INT $!
  sudo perf record -p <pid> -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 5; sudo perf report -i /tmp/perf.data > /tmp/perf-<pid>.txt

- gdb snapshot (heap / stack / mmap) for python worker (attach, bt, info proc mappings):
  sudo gdb -p <pid> --batch -ex 'set pagination 0' -ex 'thread apply all bt full' -ex 'info proc mappings' -ex 'quit' > /tmp/gdb-<pid>.bt.txt || true

- cuda-memcheck run (dev only):
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 cuda-memcheck python reproduce.py 2>&1 | tee /tmp/cuda-memcheck.txt

Common failure signatures I've seen:
- sudden OOM during KV cache decode: python worker shows big spike in rss and GPU memory freed not matching nvml used_memory -> symptomatic of mismatched libcuda (wrong ioctl size) or stale NVML binding.
- attach mismatch: libcuda from host differs from libcuda inside container (LD_PRELOAD used by earlier startup). Look for multiple libcuda.so.* paths in /proc/<pid>/maps.
- relocation failure at model load: "invalid ELF header" or undefined symbol in dlopen -> sign of mixed driver/library versions after node driver upgrade.
- soft OOM (process killed by kernel/kubepods): dmesg shows "oom_reaper" for pid with container cgroup.

Hypotheses checklist (tick during incident):
- [ ] driver upgraded in last 48h on node (check /var/log/apt/history.log or gpu-driver-deploy job)
- [ ] container image pinned to different CUDA toolchain than host
- [ ] LD_PRELOAD or custom CUDA hooks in entrypoint
- [ ] node has stale nvidia modules (modprobe mismatch) after kubelet restart
- [ ] MPS / MIG slices active causing memory accounting differences

Incident breadcrumb example (short):
- 2026-02-12T07:14 UTC: alert: infra-worker-03 high-gpu-mem usage -> jobs started failing with OOM
- 07:15: nvidia-smi snapshot: driver 525.85.05, mem 24GB total, used ~23.8GB across 5 pids -> suspicious single process using 20GB
- 07:16: attached to PID 21454 (python): environ shows LD_PRELOAD=/opt/debug/libinterpose.so (weird) -> removed preload, restart fixes 1 job but other jobs still OOM
- 07:22: dmesg shows NVRM: GPU at fault: failed to allocate mapping table (pagefault) -> suspected ABI/driver mismatch after rolling upgrade at 02:00
- 07:35: reproduced locally by docker run with host driver mismatch -> adding explicit libcuda path in container fixed (workaround)

Notes on subtle checks (less obvious):
- ARTIFACTS: trace of /var/log/nvidia-installer.log can show leftover alternate libs after partial driver install.
- If ldconfig caches point to wrong lib, run 'sudo ldconfig -v | egrep libcuda' and inspect /etc/ld.so.conf.d/* entries.
- Watch out for symbolic links: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> /usr/lib/nvidia-XXX/libcuda.so.XXX. Docker volumes that mount /usr/lib/nvidia-* can hide updates.

Recovery tactics (fast):
- kill offending process, drain node, restart kubelet after ensuring modules match (schedule maintenance).
- container-level workaround: mount host libcuda that matches driver (short term): docker run -v /usr/lib/nvidia-<ver>:/usr/local/nvidia/lib ... but document until stable.
- long-term: enforce driver+toolkit mapping in node upgrade playbook, enhance cluster admission webhook to check image toolkits vs node drivers.

Open TODOs (for follow-up):
- add a small daemon that collects /proc/*/maps every 5s when high GPU usage detected (helps find libmix).
- add automated check in jobs to fail fast if LD_PRELOAD points to anything outside /usr/local/lib (policy).
- ticket GH:redwood-infra/serving#4821 to add mem pressure sim harness for KV cache scenarios.

Random snippets captured during triage (raw):
- "E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:xx] failed to allocate device memory: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY"
- "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus" (rare)
- "cudaGetDeviceProperties returned 30" -> indicates driver incompatible error code mapping

If you read only one thing: capture /proc/<pid>/maps + tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<pid>/environ + nvidia-smi snapshot. Those three give most of the clues for lib mismatches vs real allocation exhaustion.

Scratchpad end — will iterate after next incident.
